text: Unfortunately, in real world, we do not have only transmitter and receiver, but we may have many transmitters transmitting simultaneously, on the same frequencies, and the receiver. So the receiver will get not just the useful signal that it wants to receive, but unfortunately it will get only the signals coming from the other transmitters. So think for example of WiFi. You may be on a on a street in a in a Shanghai, and you may receive the signal if you are in a in a mall, for example, from the access point of Starbucks whatever that is the access point you would like to receive from, because you are there drinking the coffee, but you will receive also the signal coming from the access points of other nearby coffee shops or shops. So your WiFi card that is a receiver in that case will get the useful signal from the Starbucks access point, but will also get the signal coming from the nearby coffee shop access point. That is an interference. Other examples are when we have transmitters that are using different technologies. So interference may come from transmitters using the same technology, like in the previous examples, all of them were WiFi access points, but.
